# Methods

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:methods` from src/data/modelRegister.ts, docs/validation/preregistered/ and docs/validation/recorded-verdicts.json. Edit those, not this file. -->

Research, not validated advice. One note per model and signal: what it says, the rule, what it reads, where it shows, how it is
tested, its pre-registered backtests and the verdicts recorded from real runs. A verdict comes only from a test whose
rule, sample and pass mark were fixed and hashed before it ran; a failed rule is never tuned until it passes (a
changed rule is registered as a new, labelled re-test). Passing a backtest is not independent model validation.

The live verdicts are in Menu > Models & validation, read from `data/local/validation/results.json` on the computer
that ran them; they win over the recorded verdicts here, which are copied from the owner's runs.

**Method 1** counts each case as independent. **Method 2** redraws whole calendar years of cases together 4,000
times (fixed seed), reports a 90% range for the lift and a p-value, and asks that the lift is positive in at least
half the series with five or more cases. A p-value of 0.00025 is the smallest 4,000 redraws can give.

## Evidence grades

A recorded verdict is never changed. A test that passed also carries an evidence grade in the app (the badge beside the panel and Menu > Models & validation), read from the correction across all tests on record and the forward record on the computer that runs the app:

- **Validated** (green): passed its pre-registered test and still holds after the Holm correction across every test on record; or, failing that, 24 months of forward record with at least 12 scored calls beat the test's own base rate (one-sided binomial p at or under 0.05).
- **Provisional pass** (amber): passed alone but not after the correction. A single-test p of 0.05 is too lax once many rules have been tried (Harvey, Liu and Zhu 2016).
- **Under review** (amber): once 12 or more forward calls are scored, the forward hit rate is below the base rate.
- **Withdrawn** (red): the forward hit rate is significantly below the base rate (one-sided binomial p at or under 0.05). It stays withdrawn until a new pre-registered version passes.
- **Review due** (amber): the test last ran more than 12 months ago.

The grades follow the practice of model-validation teams: pre-registration and no re-tuning after a fail; correction for multiple testing; out-of-sample confirmation; ongoing monitoring with green, amber and red zones (as in the Basel Committee's 1996 backtesting framework); and periodic revalidation and outcomes analysis (the Federal Reserve and OCC guidance on model risk management, SR 11-7, 2011). Backtest figures are hypothetical results and are labelled so, net of the registered costs where a test has costs, in the way the SEC marketing rule and the GIPS standards treat hypothetical performance. The grade is a research label, not investment advice.

## Models and signals

### Policy rule check (Taylor gap)

- **Says:** Policy is tight, neutral or loose against a simple Taylor rule.
- **Rule:** Rule rate = 2% + inflation + 0.5 x (inflation - target) + 0.5 x output gap; tight or loose when the policy rate is more than the band away.
- **Reads:** BIS policy rate, monthly inflation (else IMF WEO), central bank target, IMF output gap
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (Central Bank Watcher Agent), Council chat, Replicate a rate decision
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Backtest failed (version 2, recorded 2026-11-06)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (taylor_gap v1): does a tight (loose) reading come before a cut (hike) within 6 months more often than in any month, from 2000, with inflation lagged 2 months and each bank's target as it stood then? The backtest leaves out the output gap.
- **Limits:** r* fixed at 2%; output gap is an annual IMF estimate revised each vintage; targets are hand-entered.
- **Code:** `src/utils/taylorRule.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/taylor_gap.json`, registered 2026-11-05, method 1, cases counted as independent, sample from 2000-01). When the policy rate sits more than 1 point above a simple Taylor rule (tight), the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than in any month; when it sits more than 1 point below (loose), it hikes within 6 months more often than in any month. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05. SHA-256 0dcd2ef9ac2917a3…
- Version 2 (`docs/validation/preregistered/taylor_gap.v2.json`, registered 2026-11-05, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 2000-01). With an output gap in the rule, when the policy rate sits more than 1 point above it (tight) the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than in any month, and when it sits more than 1 point below (loose) it hikes within 6 months more often than in any month; the edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most countries. A re-test of version 1, which failed (61 of 161 = 37.9% against 34.8%, lift 3.1 points, p 0.23); what changed: Adds the output-gap term of Taylor (1993), 0.5 x gap, that version 1 left out and listed as its first known limit. The gap is the app's real-time estimate (one-sided Hodrick-Prescott, lambda 100, on IMF real GDP growth outturns up to each year), and year t is used only from April of t+1. Everything else is as in version 1, and the verdict is by method 2. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 eab6b716189c7258…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-05T22:50Z: **Failed** (method 1). 61 of 161 (37.9%) against a 34.8% base rate; lift 3.1 points, p 0.23; 13 series, 2000-02 to 2026-02.
- Version 2, 2026-11-06T02:31Z: **Failed** (method 2). Re-test adding the real-time output gap: lift 4.8 points, p 0.149, above the 0.05 pass mark.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: No output gap: the IMF estimate is annual and revised each vintage, so the rule here is rate = 2% + inflation + 0.5 x (inflation - target).
- v1: Inflation is today's OECD vintage, lagged 2 months to roughly what was published; revisions are not undone.
- v1: The dated target table (src/data/inflationTargetHistory.ts) is part of this test; a country is tested only in months with a confirmed published target.
- v1: Turkey, pegged currencies and banks without a numeric target are left out.
- v1: Years of rates near zero make 'loose' readings common and long; only the first month of each run counts as a call.
- v1: Cases are treated as independent in the p-value; calls in one country are separated by at least one month with a different reading.
- v2: Re-test of a failed rule: version 1 failed, and this version was written after seeing that result. The change is the term version 1 named as missing, with the textbook weight, not a weight chosen to fit.
- v2: The output gap is annual and lagged: in a month of year t+1 before April, the latest gap is for year t-1. Gaps from GDP alone are rough and the newest year moves most.
- v2: GDP growth and inflation are today's vintages: the filter uses only past years, but revisions to past data are not undone.
- v2: Neutral real rate fixed at 2% for every country, as in version 1; emerging markets with higher neutral rates read loose more often.
- v2: Same dated target table, exclusions (Turkey, pegs, no numeric target) and first-month-of-run calls as version 1.

### Leading-indicator turn to policy move

- **Says:** After an OECD leading-indicator peak (trough), the central bank tends to cut (hike).
- **Rule:** Each CLI turning point is matched with a policy move in the matching direction within 6 months.
- **Reads:** OECD composite leading indicator (via DBnomics), BIS policy rates
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (Signal track record), Timing Agent
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Backtest failed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-05)
- **How it is tested:** Hit rate against the base rate of policy moves in any 6-month window, over the full CLI history per country, turns dated only with data available at the time.
- **Limits:** Turning points are dated with hindsight today; the OECD mirror lags 5 to 6 months.
- **Code:** `src/utils/signalRecord.ts, src/utils/oecdCli.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/cli_turn_policy.json`, registered 2026-11-05, method 1, cases counted as independent, sample from 1995-01). After an OECD leading-indicator peak (trough), the central bank cuts (hikes) within 6 months more often than it does after any month. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05. SHA-256 a991477f71db0592…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-05T22:36Z: **Failed** (method 1). 96 of 351 turns (27.4%) came before a policy move the expected way, against a 35.6% base rate; lift -8.3 points. Banks kept moving the same way after leading-indicator turns.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: The leading indicator is today's vintage: the OECD revises past months, so turns are dated with some hindsight.
- v1: A turn is two months one way then two months the other (the app's own rule), dated when the second month after it is published.
- v1: Every country the app covers with both a BIS monthly policy rate and an OECD leading indicator is pooled; countries with pegs or long holds lower the base rate.
- v1: Cases are treated as independent in the p-value; turns in the same country are months apart, but global cycles make countries move together.

### Crowded futures positioning to unwind

- **Says:** Leveraged-fund positioning in the top or bottom 10% of its range tends to unwind.
- **Rule:** Entry into the 3-year top or bottom decile counts as crowded; an unwind is a 3-point move of open interest back within 8 weeks.
- **Reads:** CFTC Traders in Financial Futures, weekly
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (Futures positioning, Signal track record), Timing Agent
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Backtest passed (version 2, recorded 2026-11-06)
- **How it is tested:** Rolling bands built only from past weeks (no hindsight), unwind rate against the rate after any random week, on CFTC history back to 2006.
- **Limits:** Bands use the whole 3-year sample today (hindsight); only currencies with CME futures.
- **Code:** `src/utils/cftcPositioning.ts, src/utils/signalRecord.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/cftc_crowding.json`, registered 2026-11-05, method 1, cases counted as independent, sample from 2007-06-01). When leveraged-fund positioning in a currency future becomes crowded (top or bottom 10% of the past three years), it comes back by 3 points of open interest within 8 weeks more often than after any week. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05. SHA-256 d2f50657b535fe15…
- Version 2 (`docs/validation/preregistered/cftc_crowding.v2.json`, registered 2026-11-05, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 2007-06-01). When leveraged-fund positioning in a currency future becomes crowded (top or bottom 10% of the past three years), it comes back by 3 points of open interest within 8 weeks more often than after any week, and the edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most currencies. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 f7d9a4599a2f16df…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-05T22:36Z: **Passed** (method 1). 195 of 228 crowded weeks unwound (85.5%) against 65.8% after any week; lift 19.8 points, p 1.3e-11 with cases counted as independent; 6 currency futures, 2007-06 to 2026-09.
- Version 2, 2026-11-06T02:31Z: **Passed** (method 2). Lift 19.8 points, 90% range 15.7 to 23.8, p 0.00025 (the smallest value 4,000 year-block redraws can give), positive in 6 of 6 currencies.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: Only currencies with a CME future in the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report.
- v1: Bands use only the weeks before each week (no hindsight), so the first year of each future is not tested.
- v1: An unwind is measured in positioning, not in the exchange rate: it says crowding eases, not that the currency moves.
- v1: Cases are treated as independent in the p-value; entries the same way in one future are at least 8 weeks apart.
- v2: Same rule, sample and pass mark as version 1, which passed under method 1 (85.5% vs 65.8%, p 1.3e-11 with cases counted as independent). Version 2 changes only how sure the result is allowed to look.
- v2: Crowded weeks are extreme by construction, so part of any unwind is ordinary reversion to the middle; the base rate after any week does not remove that.
- v2: An unwind is measured in positioning, not in the exchange rate: it says crowding eases, not that the currency moves.
- v2: Six USD crosses move together; resampling whole years covers cases in the same year, not the size of the common dollar factor within a year.

### Real exchange rate gap and carry-to-volatility

- **Says:** The currency is strong (dear) or weak (cheap) against its own 10-year average, and whether carry pays for its swings.
- **Rule:** BIS real broad effective rate against its 10-year average; policy-rate gap over the US divided by 3-month realised volatility.
- **Reads:** BIS real effective exchange rates (monthly), BIS policy rates, ECB reference rates (Frankfurter)
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (FX Valuation Agent, carry in the Relative Value Agent), Council chat
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Not validated
- **How it is tested:** Does a gap beyond one standard deviation narrow over the next 12 months more often than not, on BIS REER history since 1994, using only the average known at the time?
- **Limits:** A 10-year average is a yardstick, not a fair value; real rates can trend for years.
- **Code:** `src/utils/fxValuation.ts`

### Shock early warning

- **Says:** Where external pressure is building (watch or alert), not that a shock will happen.
- **Rule:** Stated thresholds: debt due over reserves, reserves falling, import cover, external gap, terms-of-trade swing.
- **Reads:** World Bank QEDS, BIS debt securities, IMF reserves and balance of payments, World Bank Pink Sheet, UN Comtrade
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (Shock early warning)
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Not validated
- **How it is tested:** Alerts against a dated list of external crises (IMF programmes, sharp currency falls, defaults) over 2000 to 2024, with hit and false-alarm rates fixed in advance.
- **Limits:** Thresholds are rules of thumb; several inputs are annual or quarterly and published late.
- **Code:** `src/utils/shockWatch.ts`

### Where data and price disagree (ranking)

- **Says:** Ranks countries by the size of the gap between what the data say and what markets price.
- **Rule:** Size of each rule’s gap (policy, CDS, real yield, refinancing, FX) times how far its figures can be trusted.
- **Reads:** The readings above
- **Shows in:** MarketEdge disagreements, Compare
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Not validated
- **How it is tested:** Tested through its parts: a ranking can only be validated once the rules it ranks have passed.
- **Limits:** Inherits every limit of the rules it combines.
- **Code:** `src/utils/divergences.ts`

### Growth and inflation quadrant

- **Says:** Whether growth and inflation are rising or falling, per country.
- **Rule:** CLI change over 6 months and the change in y/y inflation over 3 months; above zero is up.
- **Reads:** OECD leading indicator, monthly inflation
- **Shows in:** Compare
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Backtest failed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-06)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered backtest (docs/validation/preregistered/regime_quadrant.json): both up = a hike within 6 months, both down = a cut, against the base rate, judged by method 2.
- **Limits:** Uses the latest months, which are revised.
- **Code:** `src/utils/regimeQuadrant.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/regime_quadrant.json`, registered 2026-11-06, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 1995-01). When growth and inflation are both rising (the leading indicator up over 6 months and y/y inflation up over 3 months), the central bank hikes within 6 months more often than after any month; when both are falling, it cuts within 6 months more often than after any month. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 28f7aab1c7eb0634…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-06T02:31Z: **Failed** (method 2). Lift 2.7 points, p 0.23.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: The quadrant is the app's own rule (src/utils/regimeQuadrant.ts): above zero is up on each axis. Only the two matching quadrants make a call; growth up with inflation down, and growth down with inflation up, make none.
- v1: The leading indicator and inflation are today's vintages, lagged 1 and 2 months to roughly what was published; revisions are not undone.
- v1: Every country with a BIS monthly policy rate, an OECD leading indicator and OECD inflation is pooled; pegs and long holds lower the base rate.
- v1: A call is the first month of a run of the same reading; calls in one country are at least a month apart, and runs can be short when the axes sit near zero.

### Cycle clock

- **Says:** Where each country sits in its policy and business cycle, and the next decision date.
- **Rule:** Runs of BIS policy moves, OECD leading-indicator phase, official calendar.
- **Reads:** BIS policy rates, OECD leading indicator, official central bank calendars
- **Shows in:** Research > Markets & signals (Cycle clock), Timing Agent
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Backtest passed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-06)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered backtest (docs/validation/preregistered/cycle_clock.json): once it reads hiking (cutting), another hike (cut) within 6 months, against the base rate, judged by method 2.
- **Limits:** About two years of policy history; the calendar is updated by hand.
- **Code:** `src/utils/cycleClock.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/cycle_clock.json`, registered 2026-11-06, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 1995-01). Once the cycle clock reads hiking (a hike after a hold or a cut), another hike follows within 6 months more often than a hike follows any month; once it reads cutting, another cut follows within 6 months more often than a cut follows any month. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 75fe942928029a51…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-06T02:31Z: **Passed** (method 2). Lift 35.8 points, positive in 24 of 24 countries. Caveat: it confirms that rate moves come in runs; it is not an edge over a forecaster who already expects the next move.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: The idea was suggested by the leading-indicator test (cli_turn_policy v1), which failed because banks kept moving the same way after a turn. This is a new rule written after seeing that, not a re-test of it.
- v1: Hiking or cutting uses the app's own clock (src/utils/cycleClock.ts): the latest move in the past 6 months sets the state, and 6 months without a move is on hold.
- v1: Policy rates only (BIS monthly, end of month); a hike and a cut in the same month net out. Every BIS area is pooled, pegged currencies included.
- v1: Rate cycles are well known to come in runs, so a pass says the clock reads that, not that it beats a forecaster.

### Timing Agent

- **Says:** Lines up dated catalysts, cycle, positioning, news, odds and flows for when something might play out.
- **Rule:** Collects dated facts from the sources listed; gives no probability.
- **Reads:** Official calendar, BIS, OECD, CFTC, GDELT, Polymarket, TIC, official 10Y yields
- **Shows in:** Council chat
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Backtest passed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-06)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered backtest of its one call, the unwind setup (docs/validation/preregistered/timing_agent.json): crowded and turning = a further 3-point unwind within 8 weeks, judged by method 2. The dated facts it lists make no call.
- **Limits:** Only as current as each feed.
- **Code:** `src/utils/timingAgent.ts`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/timing_agent.json`, registered 2026-11-06, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 2007-06-01). When the Timing Agent flags an unwind setup (leveraged-fund positioning in a currency future crowded, top or bottom 10% of the past three years, and already 3 points of open interest back over 4 weeks), positioning comes back a further 3 points within 8 weeks more often than after any week. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 abc80cc6cbb282a1…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-06T02:31Z: **Passed** (method 2). Lift 21.4 points, 90% range 13.4 to 29.0, positive in 6 of 6 currencies.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: This tests the agent's one call, the unwind setup (src/utils/timingAgent.ts, CFTC_TURN_PTS = 3). The rest of the agent lists dated facts (calendar, cycle, news tone, odds, flows) and makes no call to test; GDELT and Polymarket have too little saved history.
- v1: Bands use only past weeks (no hindsight). An unwind is measured in positioning, not in the exchange rate.
- v1: A position already 3 points off its extreme is partly mean reversion in progress; the base rate after any week does not remove that.
- v1: Six USD crosses move together; method 2 groups cases by year, not by the common dollar factor within a year.

### Council summary (AI synthesis)

- **Says:** The answer to your question, written by your AI model from the agents’ documents.
- **Rule:** AI model (Ollama or Gemini) with every number traced to an agent’s figure and every stance word checked; failing sentences are removed and shown.
- **Reads:** The agents’ documents only
- **Shows in:** Council chat, Reports
- **Use:** Decision input
- **Status:** Model-assisted, not validated
- **How it is tested:** Not testable as a rule. Checks: number trace, stance check; each answer is in the audit log with its model and figures.
- **Limits:** Wording and emphasis are the model’s; a different model can lean differently on the same figures.
- **Code:** `server.ts (synthesiseAnswers), src/utils/askCouncil.ts, src/utils/stanceCheck.ts`

### GDP nowcast (bridge equation)

- **Says:** Where real GDP growth is likely to come in for quarters not published yet.
- **Rule:** q/q real GDP growth on the quarter's activity-index growth and/or leading-indicator change plus last quarter's growth; months not out yet are an AR forecast of the monthly series.
- **Reads:** OECD quarterly national accounts (via DBnomics), BCB IBC-Br, Eurostat industrial production, OECD composite leading indicator
- **Shows in:** Research > History & data (Nowcast and forecasts), Council chat (Nowcast & Forecast)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Forecast evaluation passed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/forecasts/gdp_nowcast.json): nowcast made 30 days after each quarter from 2008 against the historical mean; relative RMSE at most 0.9, year-block p at most 0.10, better in half the countries.
- **Limits:** Fixed release lags, today's data vintage; OECD figures via DBnomics run about five months behind.
- **Code:** `src/utils/nowcast.ts`

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Passed** (forecast evaluation). Against the historical mean, 1 quarter ahead: relative RMSE 0.896 (90% range 0.876 to 0.924), better in 28 of 35 series; 2007-Q4 to 2025-Q4.

### Forecasts with fan charts (AR models)

- **Says:** Where GDP growth, inflation, the policy rate and government debt may go over the next one to eight quarters, with bands.
- **Rule:** AR models with the lag order chosen by BIC: GDP q/q growth, monthly y/y inflation, monthly policy-rate changes (no drift), yearly debt changes; 50/70/90% bands from the forecast error.
- **Reads:** OECD quarterly national accounts and CPI (via DBnomics), BCB IPCA, Eurostat HICP, BIS policy rates, IMF WEO debt
- **Shows in:** Research > History & data (Nowcast and forecasts), Council chat (Nowcast & Forecast)

Inflation (last 10 years) and debt (no drift) are re-tested as version 2 after version 1 failed; version 1 stays on record.
- **Limits:** Bands leave out parameter uncertainty; today's data vintage; not compared with past IMF forecasts yet.
- **Code:** `src/utils/forecasts.ts`

### Fiscal reaction (Bohn test)

- **Says:** Whether the primary balance has risen with debt in this country's own history.
- **Rule:** OLS of the primary balance on last year's debt and the output gap, outturn years only, Newey-West errors (Bohn 1998); needs 15 years.
- **Reads:** IMF Fiscal Monitor primary balance, IMF WEO gross debt, the app's output gap estimate
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Fiscal reaction)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: it summarises the past and makes no forward call.
- **Limits:** Short annual samples; the response can change with governments; not a forecast of future policy.
- **Code:** `src/utils/bohnTest.ts`

### Gross financing need

- **Says:** How much the government has to borrow each year: deficit plus external debt falling due.
- **Rule:** Overall deficit plus scheduled external public principal (World Bank IDS), as % of GDP; a lower bound because domestic amortisation has no free source. Benchmark 15% of GDP (IMF MAC DSA, emerging markets).
- **Reads:** IMF Fiscal Monitor balances, IMF GDP in dollars, World Bank IDS principal projections, QEDS
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Gross financing need)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: an accounting sum, no forward call.
- **Limits:** Lower bound (no domestic amortisation); IDS covers low and middle income borrowers only.
- **Code:** `src/utils/grossFinancingNeed.ts`

### Country risk scorecard

- **Says:** Governance, armed conflict, unrest and the economy side by side, each figure with its source and year.
- **Rule:** Six World Bank WGI estimates against the world average; UCDP/PRIO conflicts and UCDP deaths for the latest coded year; GDELT 1.0 unrest spikes; the Caldara-Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk index; IMF and World Bank debt, growth, inflation, current account, reserves and external debt. No overall score.
- **Reads:** World Bank WGI, UCDP/PRIO and UCDP, GDELT 1.0 event files, Caldara-Iacoviello GPR file, IMF WEO, World Bank Open Data
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Country risk scorecard)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: published figures side by side, no forward call and no weights.
- **Limits:** WGI and UCDP are yearly and lag a year or more; WGI estimates have wide margins of error; GDELT counts news reports, not events on the ground.
- **Code:** `src/utils/countryRiskScorecard.ts`

### Sanctions lists

- **Says:** How many people, firms, vessels and aircraft on the OFAC and UN sanctions lists have an address or nationality in the country, under which programmes; and a plain-text name search.
- **Rule:** Counts of list entries tied to the country by address (OFAC, UN) or nationality (UN), by list, type and programme. Name search: every word of the query in the listed name.
- **Reads:** OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List (files you download)
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Sanctions lists)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: counts from official lists, no forward call.
- **Limits:** Not a compliance screen: no aliases, fuzzy matching or 50% ownership rule. Entries without an address in a country do not count for it. EU and UK lists not read yet.
- **Code:** `src/utils/sanctionsLists.ts`

### Geopolitical risk VaR

- **Says:** How far the currency has fallen in its worst months when geopolitical risk was high, against all months, and how much of that the US rate and dollar moves explain.
- **Rule:** 95% VaR and expected shortfall of monthly currency changes in months with the Caldara-Iacoviello GPR index (world, and country where covered) at or above its 90th percentile, against all months; mean factor moves of those months put through the scenario model.
- **Reads:** Caldara-Iacoviello GPR file, ECB exchange rates, BIS policy rates
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Global shock scenarios > Geopolitical risk VaR)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: past co-movement with a news index, no forward call.
- **Limits:** Stress months cluster, so independent episodes are fewer than months; a 95% tail from 20-40 months is rough; currency only; GPR counts newspaper articles.
- **Code:** `src/utils/grVar.ts`

### Reserve adequacy (IMF ARA, partial)

- **Says:** Reserves against the IMF adequacy metric, with the usual months-of-imports and short-term debt cover.
- **Rule:** IMF ARA weights for floating and fixed regimes on exports, broad money and short-term debt (the other-liabilities term has no free source, so the ratio is an upper bound).
- **Reads:** World Bank reserves, short-term external debt, broad money, exports, GDP
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Reserve adequacy)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: a ratio against a published metric, no forward call.
- **Limits:** Upper bound; FX regime not chosen, both weightings shown; annual data.
- **Code:** `src/utils/reserveAdequacy.ts`

### Inflation after rate changes (local projections)

- **Says:** How inflation has moved in the months after a one-point policy rate change, in this country's history.
- **Rule:** Jordà local projections of monthly CPI y/y on the policy rate change, horizons 0 to 24 months, 3 lags, Newey-West bands.
- **Reads:** BIS policy rates, monthly CPI
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Inflation after rate changes)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: reduced-form co-movement, not the effect of policy and not a forecast.
- **Limits:** Rate moves respond to inflation, so the sign can be the reverse of the causal effect.
- **Code:** `src/utils/localProjections.ts`

### Policy rule family

- **Says:** The policy rate against five published rules (Taylor 1993, balanced, inflation only, inertial, first difference): inside, above or below their range.
- **Rule:** r* 2%, the bank's target, IMF output gap (else the app estimate); above or below when the rate is more than 1 point outside the range of the rules.
- **Reads:** BIS policy rate, monthly inflation, central bank target, output gap
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Policy rules)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Backtest too few cases (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (rule_family v1, docs/validation/preregistered/rule_family.json): does a reading above (below) every rule come before a cut (hike) within 6 months more often than after any month, from 2000, inflation lagged 2 months, targets as they stood, real-time output gap, whole years resampled (method 2); Holm across all tests on record.
- **Limits:** r* fixed; output gap revised each vintage; targets hand-entered.
- **Code:** `src/utils/ruleFamily.ts, src/utils/backtest.ts (ruleFamilyCases)`

**Pre-registered tests**

- Version 1 (`docs/validation/preregistered/rule_family.json`, registered 2026-11-06, method 2, whole years resampled, sample from 2000-01). When the policy rate sits more than 1 point above every rule in the Policy rules panel (Taylor 1993, balanced approach, inflation only, inertial 0.85, first difference), the central bank cuts within 6 months more often than after any month; when it sits more than 1 point below every rule, it hikes within 6 months more often than after any month. The edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most countries. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 10 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, a positive lift in at least 50% of series, at least 8 years. SHA-256 1fffb8f01b619ff9…

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Too few cases** (method 2). 23 cases in 10 years; method 2 needs 30 cases in 8 years. 12 series, 2000-02 to 2023-02.

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: Close to the policy rule check (taylor_gap), whose version 2 with an output gap failed; this test was written after that result. It tests the panel exactly as it reads (outside the whole range of five rules, 1-point band), with no weight or band chosen to fit.
- v1: The inertial rule (0.85 x current rate + 0.15 x Taylor) sits close to the current rate, so 'outside every rule' needs the rate far from the Taylor rule; there may be too few cases, and that verdict would stand.
- v1: The output gap is the app's real-time estimate (one-sided HP, lambda 100, on IMF real GDP growth outturns), year t used from April of t+1; the first-difference rule uses the gap of the year before that. GDP and inflation are today's vintages.
- v1: Neutral real rate fixed at 2% for every country; emerging markets with higher neutral rates read loose more often.
- v1: Same dated target table, exclusions (pegs, no numeric target) and first-month-of-run cases as the policy rule check.
- v1: A direction-of-move test, so the benchmark is the base rate of moves after any month and there is no trading cost; the signal standard's net-of-cost rule applies to return signals.

### Debt fan chart (bootstrap of past shocks)

- **Says:** The range debt could take if the next years repeat the shocks of past years.
- **Rule:** Whole past years of deviations in growth, inflation, interest and primary balance from their means are drawn with replacement onto the IMF baseline; 2000 paths; 10th to 90th percentile.
- **Reads:** IMF WEO history and projections
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Debt sustainability, fan chart)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Forecast evaluation too few cases (debt_fan_coverage version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/forecasts/debt_fan_coverage.json): the fan rebuilt at each past October IMF WEO edition (its actual years and its projections, saved in data/local/weo-vintages/) must hold the later debt outturn inside the 10-90 band 70-90% of the time at every horizon 1-5 years, whole target years resampled. Run with npm run forecast:evaluate.
- **Limits:** Past shocks only; no fiscal reaction; IMF baseline as given.
- **Code:** `src/utils/debtFan.ts, src/utils/fanCoverage.ts`

**Recorded verdicts**

- debt_fan_coverage, version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Too few cases** (forecast evaluation). Too few cases at 4 and 5 years ahead (needs 100 cases over 8 target years; 8 October editions saved). Outturns inside the 10-90 band (80% if calibrated): 1y 66%, 2y 64%, 3y 60%, 4y 55%, 5y 48%; misses mostly above the band. 179 series, 2009 to 2018.

### Costed fiscal options

- **Says:** What a stated tightening or loosening of the primary balance would do to debt and output on the baseline.
- **Rule:** Primary balance raised by the stated size, phased in evenly; growth lower by the IMF bucket multiplier range x each year's step; debt from the identity.
- **Reads:** Debt sustainability baseline (IMF WEO), IMF fiscal multiplier buckets
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Debt sustainability, costed options)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: a stated what-if on stated assumptions, not a forecast or a recommendation.
- **Limits:** Multiplier range is a guide, not estimated for the country; no confidence or interest-rate feedback.
- **Code:** `src/utils/costedOptions.ts`

### Global shock scenarios

- **Says:** How the currency and policy rate have moved with the US policy rate, the dollar, US financial stress (index of your choice) and global supply chain pressure, applied to a stated shock.
- **Rule:** OLS on monthly changes over the last 15 years; implied move = coefficients x stated shock, 90% band from Newey-West errors.
- **Reads:** ECB reference rates, BIS policy rates (incl. US), St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index or Chicago Fed NFCI / adjusted NFCI (FRED), NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Global shock scenarios)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: past co-movement applied to a stated shock, not a forecast.
- **Limits:** Linear, not causal; dollar against the euro, not trade-weighted; oil not a factor yet.
- **Code:** `src/utils/scenarioEngine.ts`

### Currency carry

- **Says:** Currencies with higher policy rates than the US have tended to pay more than they lose to depreciation.
- **Rule:** Each month, long the third of currencies with the highest policy rate gap to the US, short the lowest third, equal weights against the dollar, held a month (Lustig and Verdelhan 2007; Menkhoff et al. 2012).
- **Reads:** ECB reference rates (month-end, per USD), BIS policy rates
- **Shows in:** Models & validation (pre-registered test); no panel yet
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Signal test passed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/signals/fx_carry.json): mean monthly return net of a flat 0.25% cost per unit traded above zero (holding dollars), whole years resampled, p at most 0.05, at least 120 months over 10 years; Holm across every test on record.
- **Limits:** Policy rates stand in for money-market rates; crash risk in sell-offs; month-end fixings, not tradable prices.
- **Code:** `src/utils/fxFactors.ts`

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Passed** (signal test). Carry long-short, 321 months: 3.341% a year net of a 0.25% cost per side (gross 3.646%), 90% range 0.581 to 6.036%, Sharpe 0.451, p 0.0257 with whole years resampled; 25 currencies, 2000-01 to 2026-09. Not adjusted for the other tests run (Holm), which it may not survive.

### Currency value (five-year real depreciation)

- **Says:** Currencies that have cheapened most in real terms against the dollar over five years have tended to recover.
- **Rule:** Each month, long the third of currencies with the largest five-year real depreciation (consumer prices lagged two months), short the third with the least (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013; Menkhoff et al. 2017).
- **Reads:** ECB reference rates, BIS policy rates (for the return), OECD consumer prices
- **Shows in:** Models & validation (pre-registered test); no panel yet
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Signal test failed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/signals/fx_value.json): as carry, mean monthly net return above zero, whole years resampled, p at most 0.05; Holm across every test on record.
- **Limits:** Consumer prices only; currencies without OECD prices drop out; value pays slowly and can lose for years.
- **Code:** `src/utils/fxFactors.ts`

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Failed** (signal test). Value long-short, 265 months: -1.96% a year net (gross -0.47%), 90% range -3.905 to 0.121%, Sharpe -0.321, p 0.941; 20 currencies, 2004-01 to 2026-02.

### Currency momentum (12-1)

- **Says:** Currencies that have paid most over the past year (leaving out the latest month) have tended to keep doing so.
- **Rule:** Each month, long the third of currencies with the highest excess return over months t-12 to t-1, short the lowest third (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013; Menkhoff et al. 2012).
- **Reads:** ECB reference rates, BIS policy rates
- **Shows in:** Models & validation (pre-registered test); no panel yet
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Signal test failed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/signals/fx_momentum.json): as carry, mean monthly net return above zero, whole years resampled, p at most 0.05; Holm across every test on record.
- **Limits:** Highest turnover of the three, so the flat cost weighs most; prone to sharp reversals.
- **Code:** `src/utils/fxFactors.ts`

**Recorded verdicts**

- Version 1, 2026-11-07T00:24Z: **Failed** (signal test). Momentum long-short, 321 months: -0.868% a year net (gross 1.46%), 90% range -3.386 to 1.541%, Sharpe -0.127, p 0.716; 25 currencies, 2000-01 to 2026-09.

### Currency around rate decisions (event study)

- **Says:** How the currency has moved against the dollar in the days around its central bank's and the Fed's rate changes.
- **Rule:** Events = days the BIS daily policy rate changed; average cumulative log change of units per USD from the day before, 10 days before to 20 after, hikes and cuts apart; 90% band from resampling events.
- **Reads:** BIS daily policy rates, ECB reference rates
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Currency around rate decisions)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Description, not a tested signal: an average of past episodes, many of them expected, with no forward call.
- **Limits:** No measure of surprise (expected moves move little on the day); episodes mixed; ECB fixings, not intraday.
- **Code:** `src/utils/eventStudy.ts`

### BEER fair value of the real exchange rate

- **Says:** Whether the real effective exchange rate sits above (dear) or below (cheap) the level its fundamentals have gone with in this country.
- **Rule:** OLS of log BIS real effective rate (yearly) on log terms of trade, log GDP per head at PPP vs the US, and the summed current account (NFA proxy), Newey-West errors (Clark and MacDonald 1998).
- **Reads:** BIS real effective exchange rates, World Bank terms of trade, GDP per head at PPP, current account
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (BEER fair value)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Not validated
- **How it is tested:** Implies the gap closes. A test would ask whether a gap beyond 10% is followed by a real move toward fair value over the next two years more often than not, fitting the model only on years before each origin; not yet registered, and World Bank data are today's vintage.
- **Limits:** Levels regression on 20-30 annual points, no cointegration test; productivity vs the US, not trade partners; NFA proxied by the summed current account.
- **Code:** `src/utils/beer.ts`

### Unrest spikes (GDELT) and conflict onset

- **Says:** Months when protests or violence stand far above the country's own last two years, and whether such a year has come before armed conflict the next year.
- **Rule:** Protests and violence as a share of the country's GDELT 1.0 events each month, as a z-score against its previous 24 complete months (floor 0.25 points); a spike is z of 3 or more, an episode the first month of a run.
- **Reads:** GDELT 1.0 event files on disk, UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset
- **Shows in:** Country Research > History & data (Event history)
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Backtest failed (version 1, recorded 2026-11-07)
- **How it is tested:** Pre-registered (docs/validation/preregistered/unrest_onset.json): among country-years with no armed conflict, is a year with a spike episode followed by conflict located in the country the next year more often than quiet years in general (pooled base rate), from 2018, whole years resampled; Holm across every test on record.
- **Limits:** UCDP is yearly, so the outcome is next-year conflict, not within months; about seven recent years; pooled base rate; machine-coded news events.
- **Code:** `src/utils/unrestSpikes.ts`

In a country with no state-based armed conflict this year (UCDP/PRIO), a year with an unrest spike episode (protests or violence as a share of the country's GDELT events at 3 or more standard deviations above its own previous 24 months) is followed by armed conflict located in the country the next calendar year more often than quiet country-years in general. Pass mark: at least 30 cases, a lift of 3 points or more over the base rate, p at or below 0.05, at least 6 years. SHA-256 36191d40a31c0c32…

**Known limits, stated before the run**

- v1: UCDP's yearly files only: the outcome is armed conflict (25 or more battle deaths in the year) located in the country the next calendar year, not within 3 months as the plan first said. A monthly test would need the UCDP event dataset (GED), not on disk.

### Trade idea journal

- **Says:** How the trade ideas you logged turned out: hit rate and average currency move by idea type.
- **Rule:** Each idea (country, currency or policy rate, direction, horizon, optional invalidation, thesis, type) is fixed at entry with the latest published value and a SHA-256 hash, appended to data/local/ideas.jsonl, and scored on the first published value on or after the horizon date.
- **Reads:** ECB reference rates, BIS daily policy rates, your ideas
- **Shows in:** Menu > Idea journal; Log idea on a Council chat answer
- **Use:** Research
- **Status:** Description, not a tested signal
- **How it is tested:** Scoring, not a signal: it keeps a record of calls, it does not make them. Hit rates on a few ideas mean little.
- **Limits:** Currency moves are spot only (no carry); ECB fixings and BIS daily rates, not traded prices; the hash shows a record was changed, it does not stop a file being deleted.
- **Code:** `src/utils/ideaJournal.ts`

## Stated-method views

These show where things stand on a stated method and make no call a backtest could score.

### Output gap (app estimate)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data, Policy review Diagnose, Central Bank Watcher and Fiscal & Debt agents
- The IMF DataMapper publishes no output gap for the countries the app covers, so the app estimates one from log real GDP chained from IMF WEO real growth (NGDP_RPCH).
- Three standard filters on the same input: Hodrick-Prescott with lambda 100, Hodrick-Prescott with lambda 6.25 (Ravn and Uhlig 2002), and the Hamilton (2018) regression filter in annual form (h = 2, p = 1).
- The reading is the median of the three; the band is lowest to highest. The HP trend runs over the IMF projections to ease the end-point problem, and projection years say so.
- **Limits:** Filters on GDP alone are rough and are revised as new years arrive; the newest years move most. A stated method on official data, not an official estimate and not a forecast.
- **Code:** `src/utils/outputGap.ts`

### Debt sustainability view

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data, Policy review Diagnose, Fiscal & Debt Agent
- Public debt dynamics: d(t) = d(t-1) x (1 + i) / (1 + n) - pb + sfa, on IMF WEO debt, IMF Fiscal Monitor primary and overall balance, IMF growth and inflation. Consumer price inflation stands in for the GDP deflator, which the DataMapper does not publish.
- Five-year scenarios: the IMF path as published, a baseline on the IMF inputs with no stock-flow adjustment, ten-year historical averages, and growth, primary balance, interest rate and combined shocks shaped like the IMF standardised stress tests (2013 Staff Guidance Note), with sizes stated by the app.
- **Limits:** A view on stated assumptions, not a forecast and not an IMF DSA. Shock sizes are the app's choices, not the IMF's country calibration.
- **Code:** `src/utils/debtSustainability.ts`

### Gross financing need (lower bound)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- GFN = overall deficit + amortisation, % of GDP, from last year to five years out. Deficit = minus the IMF Fiscal Monitor overall balance; interest shown = primary minus overall balance.
- Amortisation = World Bank IDS projected principal on public and publicly guaranteed external debt (DT.AMT.DPPG.CD, all creditors) divided by IMF WEO GDP in US dollars (NGDPD) for the same year. QEDS next-12-month general government external principal is shown alongside.
- Flag: a total of 15% of GDP or more, the IMF market-access DSA benchmark for emerging markets.
- **Limits:** Domestic amortisation (local debt held by residents) has no free cross-country source, so the total is a lower bound; for countries that borrow mainly at home it can be far below the true need. IDS covers low- and middle-income countries only. IMF years from this one on and all IDS years are projections.
- **Code:** `src/utils/grossFinancingNeed.ts`

### Country risk scorecard

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Governance: the six World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators (voice and accountability, political stability, government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, control of corruption), as published estimates where 0 is the world average and 1 is one standard deviation. Within 0.25 of 0 reads as near the average; 1 or more away reads as well above or below. Change against five years earlier.
- Armed conflict: UCDP/PRIO conflicts located in the country (and how many at war level), and UCDP best estimates of state-based, non-state and one-sided deaths, for the latest year UCDP has coded, with the three years before.
- Unrest: protests and violence as a share of the country's GDELT 1.0 events in the latest complete month, as z-scores against the previous 24 months, and the spike episodes of the last 24 months (see Unrest spikes).
- Geopolitical risk: the Caldara and Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk index (AER 2022), the share of articles in ten leading newspapers about adverse geopolitical events and threats, for the country (44 countries covered) and the world, read from the authors' monthly file you save in data/local/gpr/ as .xlsx or .csv. Latest month, where it sits among all months on file, and the 12-month and all-time means.
- Economy: government debt, real growth, inflation (IMF WEO, latest outturn year, projections left out), current account, reserves in months of imports and external debt (World Bank), against five years earlier.
- No overall score: any weighting of the pillars would be a guess, and one number would look more certain than the figures are.
- **Limits:** WGI and UCDP are yearly and lag a year or more. WGI estimates are built from surveys and expert ratings and carry wide margins of error; small changes are within them. GDELT counts news reports, which rise with media attention. Figures not on file are listed as missing with the reason.
- **Code:** `src/utils/countryRiskScorecard.ts`

### Sanctions lists

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Files you download into data/local/sanctions/ (npm run sanctions:pull tries the official addresses): OFAC SDN.CSV and ADD.CSV, the non-SDN CONS_PRIM.CSV and CONS_ADD.CSV (legacy CSV layout), and the UN Security Council consolidated.xml.
- An entry counts for a country when one of its addresses is in the country (OFAC, UN) or one of its nationalities is (UN). An entry can count for several countries. Country names are matched to ISO codes by a stated table; names it cannot match are listed, never guessed.
- Counts by list and by type (people, firms and bodies, vessels, aircraft), the programmes with the most entries as the list names them, and UN entries by the year first listed.
- Name search: every word of the query (case and accents ignored) must appear in the listed name.
- **Limits:** Not a compliance screen: the lists' aliases (OFAC ALT.CSV, UN aliases) are not searched, there is no fuzzy matching, and the OFAC 50% rule (firms owned by listed persons) is not applied. Entries with no address or nationality in the country do not count for it. EU and UK lists are not read yet.
- **Code:** `src/utils/sanctionsLists.ts`

### Geopolitical risk VaR

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data > Global shock scenarios
- Stress months: the Caldara and Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk index (world; and the country index where the file has one) at or above its 90th percentile over the months that also have the currency (at least 100 overlapping months and 20 stress months).
- VaR and expected shortfall: the 95th percentile of the monthly currency change against the US dollar (100 x log change of units per dollar, month-end ECB rates; positive = weaker), and the mean change at or beyond it, in stress months and in all months.
- Global channels: the mean US policy rate and dollar moves of the stress months, put through the country's fitted scenario model (Global shock scenarios), with its 90% band from Newey-West coefficient errors.
- **Limits:** Past co-movement with a news-based index, not a forecast. GPR stays high for months at a time, so the stress months are fewer independent episodes than their count, and a 95% tail read from 20 to 40 months is rough. Currency only; no bond or equity prices. Built fresh, not ported from another tool.
- **Code:** `src/utils/grVar.ts`

### Historical context line

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data > History (under the chart)
- The latest real observation of the figure (IMF projections left out) against all earlier observations: a record high or low, or "highest/lowest since" the most recent earlier date at least as extreme, whichever run is longer.
- A "since" date is shown only when it is far enough back to matter: at least 3 years (yearly), 4 quarters, 12 months, 26 weeks or 60 days.
- Where it sits: the share of all observations at or below it. Change on the observation one year earlier, in points for shares and rates.
- **Limits:** Only the history the app has saved for that figure; a short series makes "on record" weak, so the first date is always given. No rank among peers yet.
- **Code:** `src/utils/historicalContext.ts`

### Claim check

- **Shows in:** Today > Council chat (the Claim Check answer, when a question states a figure or a ranking)
- Figures stated in the question (policy rate, inflation, government debt, primary balance, official reserves, real GDP growth) are found by the rules of the document figure check and compared with the app figure for the one watchlist country the question names, within the same tolerances (0.05 to 1 point; 2% for reserves).
- A year in the question that differs from the year of the app figure is reported as a different period, neither a match nor a difference.
- Rankings (highest, lowest, largest and so on in the G20, the G7 or the watchlist): the country's app figure is ranked against the members the app holds a figure for. A higher (or lower) figure elsewhere disproves the claim; ranking first supports it fully only when every member is covered, otherwise the uncovered members are named.
- **Limits:** A check against the app's figures, which may be older than the claim or measure something else (monthly against annual inflation, mixed sources across countries). Stated figures are checked only when the question names one country. Targets and forecasts are left out. No other groups (EM, the world) are ranked.
- **Code:** `src/utils/claimCheck.ts`

### Story leads

- **Shows in:** Research > Compare countries > Summary
- Records: the latest real observation of each official yearly series (IMF WEO, World Bank; projections left out) that is the highest or lowest on record (at least 10 observations) or since a year at least 10 years earlier, for the last two calendar years only (the Historical context line's rules).
- Revisions: values the IMF or World Bank revised in the last 30 days (Data health), by at least 0.5 points for figures in % and 5% of the old value otherwise; projections left out.
- Moved: what moved since your last visit, by the rules of Since your last visit (read only; opening Compare does not reset it). Ordered records on record first, then by how far back and how large.
- **Limits:** Only countries with saved yearly history, and only official yearly figures for records; a record in a short series means little, and the figure may be revised again. Gaps between data and market prices are in Where data and price disagree on the same page.
- **Code:** `src/utils/storyLeads.ts`

### Publication export

- **Shows in:** Research > One country > History & data > History (Publish chart, under the chart)
- The chart is redrawn on white as SVG, or PNG at twice screen size, with its title, unit and frequency, the figure's source, the period shown, the export date and a credit line.
- The credit line is the attribution each source asks for in the licence register (src/data/dataLicences.ts), with its placeholder filled from the figure's source text; it can be edited before export.
- A source whose terms restrict free sharing, or need permission where free sharing is not settled, blocks the export until you tick that you hold permission. Sources with unclear terms, or not named in the register, are listed.
- **Limits:** The register reflects terms as read on its check date and is not legal advice; you are responsible for what you publish. Only the History chart has the button so far.
- **Code:** `src/utils/creditLines.ts`

### Unit converters

- **Shows in:** Research > One country > History & data
- Real terms: amount x CPI(target year) / CPI(year of the amount), World Bank consumer price index (2010 = 100).
- US dollars: amount / official exchange rate, local currency per US$, average of the year (World Bank, from IMF IFS). Purchasing power parity: amount / World Bank ICP conversion factor for GDP. Per head: amount / mid-year population (World Bank).
- Only the year asked for is used; a year with no figure reads Missing with the years on file. IMF projections are never used.
- **Limits:** Yearly averages: a single day's amount converts only roughly, and in high inflation the year's average rate can be far from the rate on the day. The GDP PPP factor suits economy-wide amounts, not one household's basket.
- **Code:** `src/utils/unitConverters.ts`

### Exercises with answer keys

- **Shows in:** Research > One country > History & data
- Real policy rate: the BIS policy rate at the end of the month less monthly inflation (y/y) for the same month; tolerance 0.1 points.
- Taylor (1993) rule: neutral real rate 2% + inflation + 0.5 x (inflation - target) + 0.5 x output gap, with IMF WEO inflation and output gap for the year and the bank's current published target, both stated in the question; tolerance 0.1. The key also gives the actual year-end policy rate against the rule.
- r minus g: the December 10Y government bond yield less nominal GDP growth, (1 + real growth)(1 + inflation) - 1 from the IMF WEO; tolerance 0.2. Debt change: the IMF WEO government debt ratio this year less last year; tolerance 0.2.
- **Limits:** Only questions whose inputs are all on file are set; others are listed with why. IMF projections are never used. The current inflation target is used for past years. In exam mode the answer key stays on the server and answers are only marked right or not.
- **Code:** `src/utils/exercises.ts`

### Model sandboxes

- **Shows in:** Research > One country > History & data
- Debt dynamics: d(t) = d(t-1) x (1 + i) / (1 + n) - pb, with n = (1 + g)(1 + inflation) - 1, and the debt-stabilising primary balance d x (i - n) / (1 + n), the same identity as Debt sustainability. Starting values are the latest year of that panel's history (IMF WEO debt, growth, inflation, primary balance; effective interest rate where the app has one).
- Taylor rule: neutral real rate + inflation + a x (inflation - target) + b x output gap, starting from Taylor (1993): 2, 0.5 and 0.5, the latest IMF WEO inflation outturn, the bank's current published target and the app's output gap.
- Output gap: log real GDP chained from IMF WEO growth outturns less an HP trend with any lambda (100 yearly, 6.25 Ravn-Uhlig), against the Hamilton (2018) regression residual with any horizon h; at least 15 unbroken years.
- **Limits:** Illustration of the formulas, not a forecast: every term is held constant over the horizon and nothing feeds back. A starting value the app does not have reads Missing and the sandbox waits until it is set. IMF projections are never used for the filters.
- **Code:** `src/utils/modelSandboxes.ts`

### Econometrics lab

- **Shows in:** Council chat > a Chart Agent chart (ask in words, or Open larger > Tests)
- All on the rows where both of the first two series have a value, in order. Newey-West: OLS of the second series on the first with Bartlett-kernel HAC errors, lag floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)).
- VAR: both series in the chart's units, constant, lag by AIC (ln|Sigma| + 2pK^2/T) from 1 to 12 (monthly), 8 (quarterly) or 3 (yearly) on one sample; orthogonalised responses with the first series ordered first (Cholesky), over 24, 12 or 8 periods; 90% band from a seeded residual bootstrap (300 draws, 100 on samples over 1,500 points).
- Local projections (Jordà 2005): y(t+h) - y(t-1) on dx(t) and 3, 2 or 1 lags of both changes, one OLS per horizon, Newey-West errors with lag at least h + 1, 90% bands.
- Johansen (1991) trace test, unrestricted constant, VECM with the VAR's lag less one in differences; 5% critical values 15.49 (rank 0) and 3.84 (rank at most 1), MacKinnon, Haug and Michelis (1999).
- Breaks: regression of the second series on the first; sup-F, the largest Chow (1960) statistic over break dates with 15% trimming, against Bai and Perron's (2003) 5% value of 11.47; when it rejects, Bai-Perron (1998) global least squares with up to 3 breaks, the number chosen by BIC.
- **Limits:** Description, not a tested signal: none of these is a forecast or a causal estimate. VAR surprises are reduced-form, not identified shocks, and the Cholesky order matters. A VAR or regression in levels of series that wander can mislead; Johansen assumes they do wander. Break dates are estimates. Checked against statsmodels (Newey-West, VAR, local projections, Johansen) and a brute-force search (breaks).
- **Code:** `src/utils/econometricsLab.ts`

### Replication pack

- **Shows in:** Council chat > a Chart Agent chart > Replication pack
- data.csv holds the lines the chart drew, one row per date (or country, x, y for a chart across countries); trend lines the HP test adds are left out and recomputed.
- replicate.py, replicate.R and replicate.do run the tests the chart ran on the first two columns, on the rows where both have a value: correlation, OLS regression, lead/lag (up to 1.5 years of rows either way), Granger F test, rolling correlation (3 years of rows, at least 8), ADF with a constant and its lag chosen by AIC on one sample (MacKinnon 2010 critical values), the HP filter as a linear solve with the app's lambda, and where the first line stands.
- The README lists each column with its label, unit, source and credit, the settings, and the app's readings and figures to check against.
- **Limits:** A saved chart keeps its latest 600 points per line; the app ran its tests on every point, so a longer sample can give slightly different figures (the README says so when it applies). The Python and R scripts were checked against the app's figures; the Stata script follows the same steps.
- **Code:** `src/utils/replicationPack.ts`

### Reserve adequacy (IMF ARA, partial)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Traditional ratios: reserves in months of imports, reserves / short-term external debt (Greenspan-Guidotti, 100%), reserves / broad money (20%).
- IMF ARA EM metric without other portfolio liabilities: 30% of short-term external debt (World Bank IDS) + 5% (floating) or 10% (fixed) of broad money (World Bank, % of GDP x IMF WEO GDP in US$) + 5% or 10% of exports of goods and services (World Bank). Both weightings shown; reserves include gold.
- Reading: reserves under 100% of the floating-weight partial metric are under 100% of the full IMF metric whatever the regime; above that, adequacy cannot be shown without the missing term.
- **Limits:** Other portfolio liabilities (from the international investment position) have no free cross-country source, so the ratio is an upper bound of the IMF's. The exchange rate regime is not a free feed. Short-term debt is World Bank IDS, low- and middle-income countries only; annual data lag a year or more.
- **Code:** `src/utils/reserveAdequacy.ts`

### Debt fan chart (stochastic)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data > Debt sustainability
- Centred on the debt sustainability baseline (the debt identity on the IMF's projected growth, inflation, interest and primary balance), five years.
- Each simulated year draws one whole past year (bootstrap with replacement, up to the last 25 outturn years with all four inputs, at least 10) and adds that year's deviations from the sample means to the baseline inputs, so the four shocks keep their joint behaviour. Interest shocks phase in as a fifth of the debt rolls over each year.
- 2,000 paths with a fixed seed; reports the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles by year and the share of paths ending above today's debt and above the baseline. Shape of the IMF market-access DSA fan (IMF 2013).
- **Limits:** Only shocks the sample has seen; no stock-flow adjustments (valuation, bank support), which drive many debt jumps. Centred on the IMF's inputs, not an app forecast. CPI inflation stands in for the GDP deflator.
- **Code:** `src/utils/debtFan.ts`

### Inflation after policy rate changes (local projections)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Jorda (2005) local projections on monthly data: inflation (% y/y, OECD or national CPI) h months ahead less the month before, on the change in the BIS month-end policy rate in month t, with 3 lags of both monthly changes. One OLS per horizon: 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 months.
- Newey-West standard errors with lag max(h + 1, floor(4 x (n/100)^(2/9))); 90% bands. Needs 60 months and at least 5 rate changes.
- **Limits:** Reduced form: the rate change is not an identified monetary policy shock. Central banks move ahead of expected inflation, so early responses often have the "wrong" sign (price puzzle). Records co-movement in the sample, not the effect of policy; regimes and targets change over long samples.
- **Code:** `src/utils/localProjections.ts`

### Policy rule family

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Five rules on the same inputs (latest monthly inflation pi, the bank's stated target pi*, output gap, r* 2%): Taylor (1993) r* + pi + 0.5(pi - pi*) + 0.5 gap; balanced approach, gap weight 1.0; inflation only, no gap term; inertial 0.85 x current rate + 0.15 x Taylor (1993); first difference current rate + 0.5(pi - pi*) + 0.5 x change in the gap over a year.
- Output gap: IMF WEO (NGAP_NPGDP) for this year where published (a projection), else the app's own estimate, labelled. Rules needing the gap show Missing without it.
- Reading: the policy rate more than 1 point above every rule = tight on all; more than 1 point below = loose on all; otherwise inside the range.
- **Limits:** r* is a stated parameter, not data: each point lower moves the level rules one point down, the inertial rule 0.15 and the first-difference rule not at all. Rules are cross-checks of stance, not forecasts; banks also weigh the exchange rate, financial stability and expectations. Annual output gaps are revised every WEO.
- **Code:** `src/utils/ruleFamily.ts`

### Costed fiscal options

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data > Debt sustainability
- Four stated options against the debt sustainability baseline on IMF inputs: tighten 0.5 pt at once, 1 pt over 2 years, 2 pts over 3 years, loosen 1 pt at once. The primary balance rises by the step each year and stays up.
- Real growth in a step year is lower by multiplier x step (output level loss persists; later growth as baseline). Multiplier: the IMF bucket-approach first-year range for the country's group in normal times (TNM 14/04 Table 6: emerging 0.1-0.3, advanced 0.4-0.6), both ends shown.
- Debt from the identity d(t) = d(t-1)(1 + i)/(1 + n) - pb, so interest falls with debt. Reports debt at the horizon, the change against the baseline and the output lost; flags when debt rises above the baseline in year 1 (denominator effect).
- **Limits:** No cycle or lower-bound adjustment to the multiplier, no confidence or risk-premium effects, inflation and interest as in the baseline. Composition (spending or taxes) is not modelled. Stated options on stated assumptions, not a forecast or a recommendation.
- **Code:** `src/utils/costedOptions.ts`

### BEER fair value (behavioural equilibrium exchange rate)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Clark and MacDonald (1998), one country at a time: OLS of the log BIS real broad effective exchange rate (yearly average of complete years) on log net barter terms of trade (World Bank), log GDP per head at PPP against the US (World Bank, a Balassa-Samuelson stand-in), and the current account summed from its first year (a net foreign assets proxy), at least 15 years, Newey-West errors.
- Misalignment = 100 x (log REER - log fitted). The latest monthly REER is set against the fair value of the latest year with all fundamentals, and the year is stated. Coefficients whose sign is opposite to theory (all three are expected positive) are flagged.
- **Limits:** A levels regression on 20-30 annual points with no cointegration test: a yardstick, not a forecast, and it implies a gap that closes, which is not tested here. Productivity is against the US, not trade partners. Net foreign assets have no free API, so the summed current account (no valuation changes) stands in. World Bank data are today's vintage.
- **Code:** `src/utils/beer.ts`

### Currency around rate decisions (event study)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- Events: every day the BIS daily policy rate series changes (the date the new rate takes effect), its own central bank or the Federal Reserve, split into hikes and cuts; a change within 10 daily observations of the last kept one is dropped so one episode is not counted twice.
- Path: 100 x log change of units per US dollar (ECB reference rates) from the ECB business day before the event to each day from 10 before to 20 after (up = weaker currency). Average path for hikes and for cuts, 90% band from resampling the events (2,000 draws, fixed seed); at least 5 events per group.
- **Limits:** Description of the past, not a tested signal. No measure of surprise: an expected decision moves little on the day. Episodes with very different causes are averaged. ECB daily fixings, not intraday prices; currencies the ECB does not publish have no study.
- **Code:** `src/utils/eventStudy.ts`

### Unrest spikes (GDELT) and conflict onset

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data (Event history)
- Each complete month (daily files covering the month), protests (CAMEO root 14) and violence (roots 18 to 20) as a share of the events GDELT 1.0 places in the country or names it as an actor. z = (share - mean of the previous 24 complete months) / max(their standard deviation, 0.25 points). A spike is z of 3 or more; an episode is the first month of a run of spikes. Only earlier months enter the baseline.
- Pre-registered test (unrest_onset v1): every country-year from 2018 with at least 10 scored months and no state-based armed conflict located in the country (UCDP/PRIO). A year with a spike episode is a call that conflict is located in the country the next calendar year. Base rate: the share of all such quiet country-years followed by conflict, pooled. Method 2: whole years resampled, p at most 0.05, a lift of at least 3 points, 30 cases over 6 years.
- **Limits:** UCDP files are yearly, so the outcome is the next calendar year. GDELT on disk starts in 2016, leaving about seven scored years. The pooled base rate mixes countries with very different risks. News-based machine coding, with coverage that varies by country and year.
- **Code:** `src/utils/unrestSpikes.ts`

### Trade idea journal

- **Shows in:** Menu > Idea journal
- An idea is a country, an instrument (its currency against the US dollar from ECB reference rates, or its policy rate from BIS daily data), a direction, a horizon of 7 to 730 days, an optional invalidation (currency ideas: an adverse move of that many %), a thesis and a type (carry, value, momentum, macro, policy, event, other).
- When logged the server fixes the entry level (latest published value, with its date) and the horizon date, takes the SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON and appends it to data/local/ideas.jsonl; the app never edits a record, and a changed line is shown as not matching its hash.
- Scoring: on the first published value on or after the horizon date. Currency: move = 100 x (entry / value - 1) in the idea's direction (units per USD falling = the currency strengthening), a hit when above zero; invalidated if the adverse move is reached on any ECB day first. Policy rate: up, down or unchanged against the entry. Hit rate and average currency move by idea type.
- **Limits:** Scoring, not a signal. Spot moves only, no carry or costs. Few ideas give a noisy hit rate. The hash shows a change, it does not prevent deletion of the file.
- **Code:** `src/utils/ideaJournal.ts`

### Global shock scenarios (scenario engine)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- One OLS per response on monthly changes over the last 15 years (at least 60 months): the currency (100 x log change of units per US dollar, ECB month-end) and the policy rate (BIS month-end, change in points), each on the US policy rate change (BIS), the dollar (100 x log change of euros per dollar, ECB) US financial stress (change in the index you pick: the St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index STLFSI4 by default, or the Chicago Fed NFCI or adjusted NFCI; FRED, the last weekly reading of the month) and global supply chain pressure (change in the NY Fed GSCPI, monthly).
- A scenario is a set of stated factor moves (presets: Fed +1 point, dollar +5%, both, the reverse, financial stress +1 point, stress +1 with dollar +5%, supply chain pressure +1 point; or your own). Implied move = coefficients x shock, intercept left out; 90% band from the Newey-West covariance of the coefficients. The residual standard deviation is shown as the size of a typical unexplained month.
- **Limits:** Contemporaneous co-movement, linear in the shock: not causal, and the Fed and the dollar often move for the same reasons as the country. Shocks larger than any month in the sample are flagged as extrapolation. The dollar factor is euros per dollar, not a trade-weighted index. Oil is not a factor yet (only five years of monthly prices saved); the NY Fed supply chain pressure index is not either (no checked download). The Chicago Fed NFCI is left out as a near-duplicate of the stress index. Currencies the ECB does not publish have no currency model.
- **Code:** `src/utils/scenarioEngine.ts`

### Fiscal reaction (Bohn test)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data
- OLS of the IMF Fiscal Monitor primary balance (% of GDP) on the previous year's IMF WEO government debt (% of GDP) and the app's output gap estimate: pb(t) = a + rho x d(t-1) + gamma x gap(t). IMF projection years are left out.
- Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett) standard errors with lag floor(4 x (n/100)^(2/9)). Needs 15 years; when the output gap covers fewer than 80% of them the regression runs without it and says so.
- Reading: rho above zero with p below 0.05 = the primary balance responds to debt (Bohn 1998's sufficient condition for sustainability holds in the sample); p below 0.10 = weak; otherwise no response found.
- **Limits:** A record of past behaviour on the whole sample: the response can change with governments and regimes, and short samples give wide errors. No response found does not by itself show debt is unsustainable. Not a forecast.
- **Code:** `src/utils/bohnTest.ts`

### Fiscal multipliers (cited reference view)

- **Shows in:** Research > History & data, Policy review Diagnose, Fiscal & Debt Agent
- The app does not estimate multipliers. It places a country in the IMF bucket approach (Batini, Eyraud, Forni and Weber 2014, IMF TNM 14/04) using only figures it holds, and shows the published first-year ranges (low 0.1-0.3, medium 0.4-0.6, large 0.7-1.0, Table 6) with the cycle and lower-bound adjustments from p.14.
- A characteristic the app has no data for stays "not known" and widens the range rather than being guessed.
- **Limits:** Calibrated on advanced economies; emerging and low-income countries generally sit in the low bucket. A reference, not an estimate.
- **Code:** `src/utils/fiscalMultipliers.ts`
